input: Test the thesis: GLP-1 drug adoption is a lasting volume headwind for Mondelez

output.thesis: GLP-1 drug adoption is a lasting volume headwind for Mondelez International.

evidence_for.claim: Real-world household transaction data show a relevant category-level demand shock: grocery spending fell 5.3% in the first six months after GLP-1 adoption and remained about 4% lower in months 7-12; the largest declines were in savory snacks (more than 10%), sweet bakery products (8.8%) and biscuits (6.5%). Item counts fell similarly, suggesting fewer items rather than only cheaper substitutions. As of 2026-10-14.

GLP-1 adoption and reduced indulgence purchasing are becoming mainstream: PwC reported that 21% of U.S. households included a current GLP-1 user as of May 2026, up from 9% in January 2025; 54% of surveyed users had been on the drugs for more than a year, while 61% said they were buying fewer sweet treats and 56% fewer salty snacks. As of 2026-05 for adoption and 2026-06-22 for the report.

EY-Parthenon's survey of 1,700 consumers found GLP-1 users reported 40%-60% lower consumption across snack categories and projected that adoption could reduce snack-category sales growth by as much as 3%, or up to $12 billion over 10 years. The same analysis projected U.S. adult adoption of 13%-21% over the coming decade. As of 2025-02-07; these are survey results and projections, not Mondelez-specific outcomes.

The exposure is economically relevant to Mondelez because its Q3 2026 release describes the company as a global snacking business with major biscuits and baked-snack brands including Oreo, Ritz, LU, Clif Bar and Tate's Bake Shop, plus chocolate brands including Cadbury Dairy Milk, Milka and Toblerone. As of 2026-10-29.

evidence_against.claim: Mondelez's reported Q3 2026 volume/mix increased 1.8 percentage points globally, with organic net revenue growth of 2.1%; nine-month 2026 volume/mix was also positive at 0.6 percentage points and organic net revenue growth was 2.4%. North America volume/mix was flat in Q3 and positive 0.2 points year to date, while Latin America, AMEA and developed markets were positive year to date. As of 2026-09-30.

Management said Q3 2026 results were driven by broad-based volume growth and reaffirmed at least 2% organic net revenue growth for full-year 2026. That is inconsistent with a currently visible, companywide lasting volume headwind, although management guidance is not causal evidence about GLP-1s. As of 2026-10-29.

The best available transaction evidence weakens the word 'lasting': grocery-spending reductions eased from 5.3% in months 1-6 to approximately 4% in months 7-12, the weight-loss-user effect in months 7-12 was smaller and statistically indistinguishable from zero, and roughly one-third of adopters stopped the drug during the observation period. After discontinuation, total grocery spending rebounded close to the original level within six months. As of 2026-10-14.

Cornell's summary of the same transaction-based research reports that lower spending persisted at least a year among households that continued using the medication, but effects became smaller over time; after discontinuation, effects became harder to distinguish from pre-adoption spending, and about one-third of users stopped during the study period. As of 2025-12-18.

counterarguments: The category mechanism is credible, but Mondelez's own latest operating data do not yet show a companywide volume decline: Q3 volume/mix was +1.8 points and nine-month volume/mix was +0.6 points as of 2026-09-30.

The strongest persistence evidence is conditional on continued medication use, while the transaction data show meaningful discontinuation and spending reversion. Thus, adoption can create intermittent or temporary volume pressure without creating a permanent headwind.

The GLP-1 studies are primarily U.S. household or survey evidence, whereas Mondelez operates globally; positive volume/mix in emerging markets could offset U.S. snack weakness, and the company may also mitigate pressure through portion-controlled or permissible-indulgence products.

Observed purchasing changes are not fully attributable to GLP-1 biology: Cornell notes that the study cannot completely separate medication effects from concurrent lifestyle changes, so extrapolating category-level declines directly to Mondelez's volumes is uncertain.
key_uncertainties: No opened page verifies the share of Mondelez's volume by GLP-1 user, category or geography, so the company's direct exposure cannot be quantified.
It is unknown whether any U.S. biscuit and chocolate volume weakness is being masked by pricing, mix, innovation, distribution gains or growth in non-U.S. markets.
Long-term adherence and behavior beyond 12 months remain uncertain: the available evidence shows persistence among continuing users but tapering effects and reversion after discontinuation.
It is unknown whether Mondelez's smaller packs, permissible-indulgence products or other innovation can offset lower units per GLP-1 household.
The available household studies do not fully isolate GLP-1 treatment from simultaneous changes in diet, health goals and shopping behavior.
what_would_change_the_view: Several consecutive Mondelez quarters showing negative global volume/mix, especially negative North America biscuit and chocolate volume, while GLP-1 adoption continues to rise would strengthen the thesis.
Mondelez disclosing that GLP-1 users or GLP-1-related basket changes are reducing units, repeat rates or category demand would materially strengthen the thesis.
Independent panel data showing snack and biscuit purchases remain materially below baseline beyond 12 months, including among users who remain on therapy, would support the 'lasting' claim.

A sustained return of Mondelez volume/mix to positive territory in North America despite further GLP-1 adoption, or evidence that discontinuers rapidly restore snack purchases, would weaken the thesis.
Evidence that Mondelez's portion-controlled or permissible-indulgence launches generate incremental units sufficient to offset lower consumption per GLP-1 household would weaken the thesis.
output.verdict: Partly supported, but not yet supported as a lasting companywide volume headwind. GLP-1 adoption is rising and the best available household evidence shows meaningful declines in snack and biscuit purchases, which is relevant to Mondelez's portfolio; however, those effects taper or reverse after discontinuation, while Mondelez reported positive Q3 and nine-month 2026 volume/mix and reaffirmed growth guidance. The thesis should currently be framed as a credible medium-term category risk rather than an established Mondelez volume trend.
missing_fields: Mondelez volume by GLP-1 exposure, category and geography
Mondelez-specific unit and repeat-purchase data for biscuits and chocolate
Independent evidence of snack-purchase persistence beyond 12 months among continuing GLP-1 users
